prompt:
CAMERA: 35mm cinema lens, shallow depth of field, framed from BEHIND the person at shoulder height; locked-off, then a very slow push-in over the whole shot. The camera never pulls back, never shows itself.
LOOK: match the reference frame's grade EXACTLY: dim blue-hour office, heavily desaturated near-monochrome, deep grey shadows, no daylight, no bright walls, real film grain. The ONLY colored element in the entire video is one tiny highlighter-yellow point at the raised fingertip.
STYLE: cinematic brand film, slow, held, precise. Silent except the room tone, which cuts to total silence at the freeze. No glow, no neon, no lens flare, no light particles: every dot is a matte physical grain, like a halftone made of real grains.
CHARACTER: no full person and no face anywhere. The only human presence is ONE right hand and forearm in a plain dark sweater sleeve, and it is made of thousands of small matte grey grains gathered into the shape of a hand. Same hand in every shot.
SETTING: a real hospital nurses' station at night, empty of people, a large whiteboard duty roster on the wall with many blank cells, desk, phone, printer, dim practical lights.
CONSTRAINT: absolutely no letters, words, or numbers anywhere, including on the whiteboard; existing board content is only faint abstract ticks; no readable text anywhere, no legible numbers, no letters on any screen or paper, no logos, no watermarks, no subtitles, no other colored element besides the single yellow point.
SCENES:
1. (~2s, wide, static) The empty station at night. From the left edge, thousands of small matte grey grains fly in along three thin converging pencil-like lines toward the whiteboard.
2. (~2s, slow push-in toward the board) The grains GATHER into the shape of a right hand and dark-sleeved forearm holding a marker; a tiny yellow point sits at the marker tip.
3. (~2s, close on the board) The gathered hand writes and blank cells of the roster fill in one by one with short abstract strokes and small dots only, never letters, never words, never numbers. Then the hand loosens back into grains and streams out of the right edge of the frame along the lines. One soft chalk tap sound.
